trackTitle: CBSE Class XII Information Technology (Subject Code: 802) Complete Mastery
description: A comprehensive, exam-aligned curriculum for CBSE Class XII Information Technology (Code 802) as prescribed by CBSE and tested in top institutions (e.g. Army Public School Barrackpore). Covers Database Concepts & MySQL RDBMS (DDL, DML, Joins, Aggregates), Operating Web-Based Applications & E-Services (E-Governance, E-Commerce, 4 Stages of Web Dev), Java Programming (JVM, Operators, Control Flow, Arrays, Strings, OOP & Constructors, Multithreading, Assertions), Work-Integrated Learning (WIL), and a dedicated Special Segment for Solved Question Paper Samples & School Board Sets.

segments.title: Segment 1 – Database Concepts & Relational Database Management with MySQL
segments.summary: Master relational database architecture, keys, data types, DDL schema management, DML operations, WHERE filtering, single/multi-row functions, GROUP BY aggregations, and multi-table relational joins.

modules.title: Relational Database Concepts, Keys & Terminology
topics: Introduction to Database Management Systems (DBMS) and Need over File Systems
Work Areas and Domains utilizing DBMS (Telecommunication billing, Hospitality, Banking, Education, Railways)
Relational Model Terminology: Relation (Table), Tuple (Row/Record), Attribute (Column/Field)
Calculating Degree (Number of Attributes) and Cardinality (Number of Tuples) after Table Alterations
The Concept of NULL in SQL: Unknown, Unassigned, or Not Applicable Values (Why '= NULL' Fails)
Relational Keys: Primary Key, Candidate Key, Alternate Key, Composite Primary Key
Foreign Key and Referential Integrity: Parent Table vs Dependent/Child Table Relationships
Self-Referencing Foreign Keys: When a Primary Key References a Column in the Same Table
SQL Statement Termination with Semicolon (;) and MySQL Client Navigation (`USE db;`, `SHOW TABLES;`, `DESCRIBE table;`)
Downloadable Documents
Practice your Skill here
learningOutcomes: Define relational terminology including relations, tuples, attributes, degree, and cardinality
Calculate updated degree and cardinality when columns and rows are added or deleted
Differentiate between Candidate, Primary, Alternate, and Foreign keys
Explain the semantics of NULL values in relational databases
modules.summary: Master fundamental RDBMS terminology, degree and cardinality calculations, NULL semantics, and primary/foreign key relationships.
miniProjects: Design a Relational Schema for School Teachers and Students Database (Teacher & Student tables)
Create a Telecommunication Call Detail Record (CDR) Schema with Primary and Foreign Keys

assessment.type: Schema Design Assignment + RDBMS Concepts Quiz

teachingFlow: Why DBMS is Used in Industry (Telecom, Hospitals, Schools)
The Meaning of NULL in SQL
Primary Keys & Foreign Keys in Action

modules.title: MySQL DDL Statements & Table Constraints
topics: Classification of SQL Commands: Data Definition Language (DDL) vs Data Manipulation Language (DML)
Valid MySQL Data Types: `CHAR(n)`, `VARCHAR(n)`, `INTEGER` / `INT`, `DECIMAL(p,s)` / `NUMERIC`, `DATE`, `TIME`
Deep Dive into `DECIMAL(p, s)`: Precision (Total digits) vs Scale (Digits after decimal point) - e.g. `DECIMAL(3,2)` for IMDb ratings
Creating Tables with `CREATE TABLE` and Defining Column & Table Constraints
Column Constraints: `PRIMARY KEY`, `NOT NULL`, `UNIQUE`, `DEFAULT`, `CHECK`
Foreign Key Constraint Definition and Cascade Operations (`ON DELETE CASCADE`, `ON UPDATE CASCADE`)
Modifying Live Table Structure with `ALTER TABLE`: Adding Columns (`ALTER TABLE table ADD column datatype`)
Modifying Columns, Renaming Columns (`CHANGE`), and Dropping Columns with `ALTER TABLE`
Removing Tables: Difference between `DROP TABLE` (DDL - removes schema & data) and `DELETE FROM` (DML - removes rows, rollback possible)
Viewing and Verifying Database Schema: `DESCRIBE table_name` and `SHOW CREATE TABLE`
Downloadable Documents
Practice your Skill here
learningOutcomes: Write valid CREATE TABLE statements with column constraints and foreign key actions
Calculate the maximum digits stored before and after the decimal for DECIMAL(p, s) data types
Alter live database schemas to add new columns (e.g. BloodGroup CHAR(2)) using ALTER TABLE
Contrast DDL DROP command with DML DELETE command with respect to rollback and schema destruction
modules.summary: Master SQL DDL commands: CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE ADD column, DECIMAL(p,s) precision, ON DELETE CASCADE, and DROP vs DELETE distinctions.
miniProjects: Create a Movie Database Table (`MovieName`, `Release_Year`, `Type`, `imdb_rating DECIMAL(3,2)`)
Write SQL Scripts to Alter a Student Table and Add a BloodGroup Column

assessment.type: DDL Schema Coding Lab + Precision Calculation Test

modules.title: SQL DML Statements, Data Filtering & Pattern Matching
topics: Inserting Records with `INSERT INTO table_name VALUES (...)` (Handling String, Date, and Decimal Literals)
Updating Records with `UPDATE table_name SET col = expr WHERE condition`
Arithmetic Updates: Increasing Attribute Values by Percentages (e.g. `UPDATE STOCKDATA SET Value = Value * 1.25;`)
Deleting Specific Rows with `DELETE FROM table_name WHERE condition;`
Querying Data with `SELECT` Statement: Selecting Specific Columns, Arithmetic Expressions, and Aliases
Filtering Data with the `WHERE` Clause: Relational Operators (`=`, `<>`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`)
Logical Operators in SQL: `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` and Evaluation Precedence
Pattern Matching with the `LIKE` Operator: Wildcard `%` (Any sequence of characters) and `_` (Exact single character)
Searching for Patterns: Starting with a letter (`LIKE 'A%'`), Ending with a letter (`LIKE '%a'`), Containing a word (`LIKE '%Kumar%'`)
Set Membership and Range Filtering: `IN (...)`, `NOT IN (...)`, `BETWEEN ... AND ...`
Handling NULL in Queries: Filtering with `IS NULL` and `IS NOT NULL` (e.g. `WHERE Comm IS NULL`)
Eliminating Redundant Output Rows: The `DISTINCT` Keyword in SELECT Statements
Sorting Results: The `ORDER BY` Clause (Ascending `ASC`, Descending `DESC`, Multi-Column Sorting)
Downloadable Documents
Practice your Skill here
learningOutcomes: Insert movie, stock, employee, and student records into MySQL tables accurately
Execute mass and conditional arithmetic updates using the UPDATE statement
Construct complex WHERE filters using LIKE wildcards, IN sets, and IS NULL checks
Eliminate duplicate records using DISTINCT and sort data using ORDER BY DESC
modules.summary: Master SQL DML commands: INSERT INTO, UPDATE SET arithmetic adjustments, DELETE WHERE, LIKE pattern matching, IS NULL checks, DISTINCT, and ORDER BY.
miniProjects: Build a Stock Trading Database (`STOCKDATA`) with 25% Value Appreciation Updates
Construct an Employee Information Filtering System with Pattern Matching and NULL Checks

assessment.type: SQL DML Query Lab + Query Output Prediction Test

teachingFlow: Handling IS NULL / IS NOT NULL

modules.title: SQL Aggregate Functions & GROUP BY Queries
topics: Single-Row Functions vs Multi-Row (Aggregate) Functions in SQL
Mathematical Aggregate Functions: `SUM(column)`, `AVG(column)` (Ignoring NULL values)
Extreme Value Discovery: `MIN(column)` and `MAX(column)` (e.g. `SELECT MAX(FEE), MIN(FEE) FROM COACH;`)
Counting Records: `COUNT(*)` (Total rows including NULLs) vs `COUNT(column)` (Non-null values only)
Grouping Records by Categories using the `GROUP BY` Clause (e.g. `SELECT Type, SUM(Value) FROM STOCKDATA GROUP BY Type;`)
Combining `WHERE` Filtering with `GROUP BY` Aggregations (e.g. `SELECT SUM(Salary) FROM Emp WHERE Job='Analyst' AND HireDate>'2012-01-03';`)
Filtering Grouped Data using the `HAVING` Clause vs Row-Level `WHERE` Clause
Multi-Column Grouping and Multi-Level Aggregations in Business Reporting
Downloadable Documents
Practice your Skill here
learningOutcomes: Compute summary statistics on database columns using SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, and COUNT
Group records by categorical attributes using the GROUP BY clause
Predict query outputs involving aggregate functions with compound WHERE conditions
Differentiate between WHERE (row filter before aggregation) and HAVING (group filter after aggregation)
modules.summary: Master SQL aggregate functions (SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, COUNT), GROUP BY categorical summarization, and query output prediction on EMP and STOCKDATA tables.
miniProjects: Generate Stock Portfolio Summary Reports (Buy vs Sell Totals) using GROUP BY
Build an Employee Payroll Summary Report with Date and Role Filters
teachingFlow: SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX Syntax & Execution
